A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CMPT research. Text, equations, tables, figures and appendices support reliable comparison, including matching v2 Sections S1–S7 to v3 Sections A1–A7.

before.justification: v2 reports original CMPT results across five datasets, including missing-modality experiments, modality-dropout ablations and per-class analyses.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experimental results in the main text and appendix.

M1.justification: Both use one CMPT per modality, frozen encoders with rank-1 LoRA, cross-modal alignment loss, gating and additive fusion. The new Section 3.5 heading separates an existing description of missing-modality handling without changing the procedure.

E1.justification: Both evaluate MM-IMDb, UPMC Food-101, Kinetics-Sound, AVE and CREMA-D. Complete-modality, missing-modality and mismatched training/inference availability scenarios are retained, including appendix Section S4/A4.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in Tables 1–4 and 6 and the ablation comparisons. In particular, v2's Kim et al. [20] and v3's Kim & Kim (2024) denote the same evaluated method.

E3.justification: The reported splits, encoders, preprocessing, metrics, training schedules and testing procedures match. This includes the 70% missing-rate configurations in Table 6 and the varying-availability evaluations.

E4.justification: Both retain the same modality-dropout ablations, generalization curves, per-class CMPT comparisons and modality-dependence analyses. v2 Figures 4–10 correspond to v3 Figures 3–9 without added or removed analytical evidence.

E5.justification: Both report means and standard deviations from three independent runs with different seeds in Tables 1 and 6. No repeated-run or uncertainty-reporting practice is added or revised.

E6.justification: The numerical entries in Tables 1–4 and 6 and the plotted results match. For example, Table 3 retains CMPT's 94.47% Food-101 accuracy and 63.58/69.23 MM-IMDb F1-macro/F1-micro scores. Revised radar and generalization graphics change labels and presentation, not results.

T1.justification: The dataset and token definitions, alignment objective, gating formula and total loss in Equations 1–7 are retained. The additional pretrained-encoder rationale introduces no new formal assumption, derivation or proof.

C1.justification: The v3 abstract explicitly adds that CMPTs require neither explicit modality generation nor auxiliary networks, and the introduction qualifies performance-gap bridging as partial. The principal approximation, efficiency and benchmark-performance contributions retain their scope.

C2.justification: Section 5 newly discusses the existing two-modality evaluation restriction, explains its benchmark-comparability rationale and identifies extension beyond it as future work. Section 3.1 also adds a rationale linking pretrained encoders to performance and faster convergence.

D1.justification: Section 4.2 and Table 5 retain the implementation, hyperparameter, software and hardware information. LoRA placement was already documented in v2, and both versions still promise a future release of code and pretrained models.

R1.justification: v3 adds Han et al. (2023) to support the expanded pretrained-encoder discussion and adjusts some citation placements. The main related-work categories and positioning against existing missing-modality approaches remain intact.

P1.justification: There are localized edits to the abstract, introduction, method explanation and limitations, plus a new Section 3.5 heading for existing material. Citations become author–year references and supplementary sections become appendix sections; most prose and section order are retained.

P2.justification: The document changes throughout from two columns to a single-column layout with different typography, spacing and display placement. v2's method diagram and radar plot are combined as v3 Figure 1(a–b), while subsequent figures and appendix displays are resized or relocated.

improvement.justification: v3 provides clearer justification for pretrained encoders, makes existing missing-modality handling easier to locate, and explicitly acknowledges the two-modality scope in Section 5. These offer a limited improvement in explanation and qualification. The substantial visual reformatting accompanies unchanged scientific methods, experimental evidence and reproducibility information.
